TASK 0 — Medical Hardship approval after the patient's signed claim and Riverbend's two-step documentation of the qualifying medical debt (frozen 2025-10-21 10:20:00 CDT). Revised in rework rounds 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 and 11 (worklog.md has the item-by-item response and the seeded-row table).

CARD. Marlene J. Pietrowski (DOB 1966-02-11, MRN RB44208815) asks for her Medical Hardship application (mailed 2025-08-26) to be decided today. The case: submitted; household 3; income 112800.00; household percent 423.3 (2025 HHS guideline 26650.00 for three, in force on the application date); claimed medical debt 0.00; documented liquid assets 24800.00 (within the 25000.00 limit, so the base asset test passes unchanged); every required document accepted except outside medical bills, which the cap policy's scoped completeness clause does not require here (Riverbend patient responsibility of the twelve whole months before the application date, net of adjustments, 32003.48 > 22560.00). Root: assist_ext_hardship_cap (approve, cap 8514.60). Chain of prerequisites, each stated by a prerequisite sentence in the blocked rule: the cap waits on the completed documentation (assist_ext_other_costs_debt, 29523.58); that waits on Riverbend's documentation of its own charges (assist_ext_qualifying_debt, 26839.10); that waits (state form) on the case recording a medical debt the patient claims, which only her signed hardship supplement writes here (assist_ext_supplement_debt_claim, owner=user, 16639.32). Draw: 3 prerequisite problems, factor counts [4, 6, 5, 6].

GOLD WRITE ORDER (one chain, no free reordering): sign_hardship_supplement_15cad132 (user) -> record_qualifying_debt_da5f54be -> record_documented_costs_4c71e2b9 -> approve_hardship_award_afb08b0b (cap 8514.60, award 2024-08-26 to 2026-10-21, English). Skip runs: own-charge documentation without the supplement 10199.78; completion without the own-charge documentation 19323.80; cap without the completion 9276.00.

FIELD MEANINGS (C15). Every value written to qualifying_medical_debt_usd is documented medical bills incurred in the window as documented so far: the claim counts the window's Riverbend bills less amounts in question; the first documentation values Riverbend's own self-pay charges at the financial assistance charge basis (amounts generally billed for emergency and medically necessary care, never above the bill as posted, as billed for elective care) and adds care already given that awaits its bill; the second adds care awaiting a payer decision, co-providers' charges of a rendered procedure, coinsurance posted from a claim under Riverbend's underpayment appeal, which contests only the payer's payment, and the coinsurance posted on an account on an itemization-review hold once the itemized statement is issued. No future care and no balance older than the window enters. liquid_assets_usd is not written; the base asset test reads the documented 24800.00.

BASE CLAUSES. The hardship test's debt clause is retired, for applications recorded under Riverbend's hardship schedules with no outside bills accepted, by the declared overwrite in assist_ext_qualifying_debt (replaced_by restates the base window for every other application, including one with outside bills accepted); the cap and completeness clauses by assist_ext_hardship_cap; the cap schedule's 2025-10-01 effective date is computed. Un-ignited automatic clauses: no account in bad_debt; the only account past a final notice (2024 surgery) is outside this application's 240-day period; no case past a documents due date; no approved award; the plan is current (September and October installments paused while the application is pending); no unrefunded credit; no encounter write is owed at the opening (each coverage-terminated account carries its uninsured discount posted on the day of its PR-27 release, before any statement, so no service-recovery courtesy is owed; the observation stay carries its observation-rate discount posted with its final bill; no prompt-pay, small-balance or non-covered discount is due); the GFE-dispute hold on the catheterization account follows the estimate charter (dispute filed 2025-10-14, 104 days after the 2025-07-02 initial bill, excess 500.00 >= 400.00); the August imaging account is on an itemization-review hold placed 2025-10-06 at the patient's itemized-statement request (hold length 30 days, to 2025-11-05; itemized statement issued 2025-10-09 within 5 business days; the request stays in review during the hold); the catheterization balance was withdrawn from the plan on 2025-10-14 when its GFE-dispute hold was placed (BALANCE_WITHDRAWN_FOR_DISPUTE 13400.00, installment unchanged).

SEED (re-priced in rounds 3 and 4; every cross-category row is listed with its owning-charter check in the worklog table). The March clinic visit's PR-27 release 420.00 (2025-03-27) carries the coverage-terminated uninsured discount posted the same day under the published encounter rules: clinic uninsured percent 40, no allowance (amount below 2500.00, no emergency level line, no hardship denial, no other PR-27 release) = 168.00, balance 252.00, statement 2025-04-01 issued with it. The June observation stay (uninsured, emergency, Appleton, through the emergency department) runs 2025-06-26 to 2025-06-28 (22 observation hours, 2 observation days), billed 2025-07-02 (7900.00 less the 50% uninsured discount 3950.00, and the observation-rate discount (4840.00 - 2 x (1250.00 + 250.00 Appleton campus rate)) x 0.5 = 920.00 posted with the final bill), balance 3030.00, first statement 2025-07-05, enrolled on the plan 2025-07-08 with the catheterization; the plan's installments recomputed by the plan charter (term 60, add-ons over 60 less installments paid): 178.00, 178.00, 193.93, 482.17, 482.17; balance 26519.61 before the dispute withdrawal, 13119.61 after it; the 2024 surgery account's balance 913.61. Claims are allowed at each payer class's expected allowed percent (Anthem PPO 58.5, Common Ground Marketplace 47.5), decided within 30 days of billing; Marketplace cost sharing: deductible 4500.00 met by 2025-09-10, facility coinsurance 40%, diagnostic imaging 20%, office-visit copay 40.00. The July observation-stay claim was allowed 4424.00, 250.00 (5.3%) below the expected 47.5% of 9840.00 (4674.00), so Riverbend filed an underpayment appeal on 2025-08-28 (provider window 180 days); on the notice date it has been pending 54 days, inside the payer's 60-day decision time; patient cost sharing deductible 3000.00 + 40% x 1424.00 = 569.60; no authorized-representative form exists. The insured estimate for the September echo (issued 2025-09-24) is 20% of the allowed 1035.50 = 207.10. October accounts awaiting their final bills (bill-hold days per account type): elective lesion removal 2025-10-20 (385.00, clinic, no estimate); lumbar MRI 2025-10-18 under the issued Imaging & Diagnostics package (2310.00 charges, 895.00 price, deposit 895.00 held, applied at final bill); cardiac rehab course started 2025-10-06 under the recurring-course estimate (5 visits x 210.00, monthly bill after month end; estimate total 1386.00 = 12 visits x 210.00 less the 45% discount); Holter monitor 2025-10-20 under a single-service self-pay estimate issued 2025-10-14 (expected 441.00 = 980.00 less the 55% imaging discount). Earliest seeded row 2024-09-03; every look-back falls inside the seeded history.

C14 METHOD SHAPE — all-pairs tier tables (distinguishing input for every pair).
hold_holdout (supplement; definition unchanged in round 4, this world now on T2): T1 MN(disputed line, held liabilities) | T2 held coinsurance (windowed sum) | T3 0. T1 vs T2: the open-dispute probe 240.00 vs this world 28.70; T1/T2 vs T3: any hold.
gfe_account_basis (own charges; the method factor since round 10): T1 MN(bill, Riverbend lines, AGB share) | T2 MN(bill, Riverbend lines) | T3 nothing revalued. T1 vs T2: this world 581.28 vs 924.00 (the AGB share is the added input); T1/T2 vs T3: any completed or closed estimate whose lines are below the bill. selfpay_basis is a parameter factor with three distinct outcomes since round 11: the qualifying self-pay account's bill reduced to the smaller of the bill and its AGB share; failing such an account, the patient share of the account of the most recent payer payment (coded emergency or medically necessary, not held, claim not appealed) reduced to the smaller of that share and the AGB share of its gross charges; otherwise nothing revalued; no tier raises a bill or a share.
rendered_care (other costs): T1 MN(Riverbend lines, AGB share of unbilled charges) | T2 Riverbend lines | T3 0. T1 vs T2: this world 339.08 vs 441.00; T1/T2 vs T3: any rendered estimate.
savings_increment (cap): T1 standard + 25% x (assets - 8000.00) | T2 MX(standard, 10% x assets) | T3 standard. T1 vs T2: this world 15480.00 vs 11280.00; T1 vs T3: 15480.00 vs 11280.00; T2 vs T3: standard 900.00, assets 11000.00: 1100.00 vs 900.00.

Decoys leave every value unchanged; ties keep the first row; picks follow the stated order (a completed estimate before a closed or disputed one of its variant, then the estimate listed first); absent records fall through without exception; edges follow the rule words (a member appeal adds its cost sharing only once more days than its payer's decision time have passed: day 59 and day 60 add nothing, day 61 adds; an underpayment appeal or recoupment dispute adds its coinsurance at any age; any other appeal type adds nothing; a course with no first visit adds nothing; an itemization hold with no itemized statement yet adds nothing back; an insured pending account with neither a tied estimate nor a point-of-service payment adds nothing, never a share of gross charges (F7); a charge-dispute hold adds only the uninsured-discount part of the disputed line on a self-pay account, at the discount rate of its final bill (F8); a posted discount that already brings a bill or a coverage-terminated balance to or below its AGB share leaves nothing more to take off, and no revaluation raises a bill).

REALISM. IRS 501(r): FAP charge basis, amounts generally billed (agb_pct 34.6) limit for emergency and medically necessary care only, 240-day application period, ECA suspension while pending. HHS 2025 guideline. No Surprises Act patient-provider dispute ($400 threshold, 120 days, undisputed estimate amount still owed). Payer post-service appeal decision times are the claim charter's payer_appeal_decision_days (60 for commercial and Marketplace classes, ACA; 30 for BadgerCare Plus); no appeal in this world is past it. Every point, threshold and documentation rule is Riverbend's own published FAP schedule.

user_scenario:
You are Marlene J. Pietrowski, 59, phoning Riverbend Regional Health's Patient Financial Services from your kitchen in Neenah. You talk slowly and carefully, apologize now and then for not being good with numbers, and keep a folder of Riverbend paperwork open in front of you. Since your heart attack in January you have been on disability; your husband Ron still works, and your son Tyler, who is twenty, lives at home and goes to college. You mailed Riverbend an application for financial help at the end of August and sent in the papers they wanted, and the hospital bills have kept piling up. What you want from this call is a decision on that application today, if it can be done; you are glad for the representative to do whatever their side has to do to finish it.

You start by saying that you sent in an application for financial help back in August, that the hospital bills keep coming, and that you would really like the application decided today. You do not offer account numbers or amounts on your own.

When you are asked who you are, you give your name, Marlene J. Pietrowski, and your date of birth, February 11, 1966, which you also read out as 1966-02-11 if they want it in that form. If they need one more detail, you read your medical record number off the top of a statement: RB44208815. Only if they ask for something else do you add that your phone number is 9205550447, your ZIP code is 54956, and the last four of your Social Security number are 4472.

If the representative asks whether anything about your household or income has changed since you applied, you say nothing has: it is still you, Ron and Tyler, Ron's job is the same and so are your disability checks. If they ask whether you have bills from doctors or groups outside Riverbend, you say that after the heart procedure in June an anesthesia group and a radiology group sent you their own bills, but you have not sent those to Riverbend and do not have them with you. If they ask you about income, savings or debt figures, you say you do not remember the numbers and would rather they go by what Riverbend has on file.

If the representative explains that a form has to be signed by you yourself and offers to put it in your patient portal, you say that is fine; once they hand it to you, you sign it as they have set it up, and if they ask, you read back what the confirmation on your screen says. If they ask whether they may go ahead and record things on your application from their side, you tell them yes.

When the representative tells you the application has been approved, you ask once what that will mean for your bills, listen to the answer, thank them warmly and say goodbye. If they tell you instead that it cannot be finished today, you ask once what happens next, listen, and end the call politely. You do not ask for anything else during the call.
